problem:
Write the following first-order linear ODE in standard form.

$$
(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{x+y}{x}\,.
$$
worked_solution:
A first order linear ODE is in standard form if it is written as

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}+P(x)y=Q(x)\,,
$$

where $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ do not depend on $y.$

$$

$$

We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(\frac{1}{{x}^{2}})\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{x+y}{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{2}(\frac{x+y}{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =x(x+y) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & ={x}^{2}+xy \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}\,+{{(-x)}_{⏟}}_{P(x)}y & ={{{x}^{2}}_{⏟}}_{Q(x)} \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}-xy & ={x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, the equation is written in standard form with $P(x)=-x$ and $Q(x)={x}^{2}.$
